target_customer: Finance, marketing, operations and revenue teams, and manufacturers that process orders by hand in spreadsheets and email
problem: Teams spend hours cleaning data, matching records and moving data from emails, PDFs and Excel exports into other systems, using brittle spreadsheets and scripts.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform, with an order to ERP automation product for manufacturers described by profiles
product_category: Back office automation, spreadsheet replacement and AI order processing

founders.name: Sidney Rema
education: Partly trained as a medical doctor (institution not named)
previous_startups: Earlier company that built payments systems with over $10M monthly GTV across Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda (name not given)
founders.background_notes: YC page: five plus years in banking extending credit to micro and small businesses in Nairobi. Also listed as co-founder of Patika, the earlier name of the company.

founders.name: Phelix Juma
founders.background_notes: YC page: helped three companies build payments systems processing $10M monthly GTV across Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria; expertise in payments integration and data science.

technical_complexity.rationale: Workflow automation across thousands of app integrations and AI entity matching is standard engineering with hard parts around reliability and document parsing; the founders had payments integration experience.

defensibility.rationale: Many no code automation tools existed and AI order parsing is copyable. Stored workflows and ERP integrations give some switching cost once deployed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent absorbing the product. General AI tools later made the document extraction layer cheaper, which the company itself cites as the alternative it competes against.

market_need_then: The launch post says spreadsheets, macros and scripts are brittle and general AI tools reinvent logic each run. The company later narrowed to turning emailed, WhatsApp and PDF orders into ERP entries for manufacturers. No dated 2022 evidence of demand was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses sanifu.ai as the main domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct B2B copy focused on replacing repetitive spreadsheet work.

rebrands.why: Not stated in the sources opened. YC lists a Patika company page and aggregators say Sanifu was formerly Patika.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, community or merch was found, and search results are crowded with Zanifu, a different Kenyan company with a near identical name.

outcome_analysis: Sanifu is active with a five person team in Nairobi after the Summer 2022 batch, and appears to have been called Patika before. It has moved from a generic spreadsheet automation pitch toward AI processing of manufacturers' orders into ERP systems. No funding beyond aggregator figures, no exit and no shutdown were found, so success or failure cannot be judged from public data.
notes: Unverified: an aggregator (Yes Press) lists about $1.02 million raised with Goodwater Capital and Y Combinator, seen in one snippet only, so no round is recorded. Founding year is 2021 per the YC page; one source says the sanifu.ai product launched in August 2024 after about three years of R&D. Zanifu is a different company and its $1M and $11.2M rounds must not be attributed to Sanifu. The competitor searches returned only 2026 era listicles, and the launch post names no rivals, so no competitor dated near the June 2022 batch is recorded. Sidney Rema's other affiliation, Patika, is the earlier company name.
